messages.author: 44606c2abd4c1731
messages.subject: meanspec() units and usage
parts:
Hello!

Hello!
I am working on a project where I would like to compare the spectral distribution of energy before and after the playback of a predator cue.

From the long recording, I extract am extracting one chunk of sound before the event occurs ("Before_event") and a second chunk of sound from after the event occurs ("After_event"). To extract the spectral information from these recordings, I am using the following code

before_spec<-meanspec(Before_event, f=300000, ovlp=90, plot=FALSE, dB=NULL, norm=FALSE)
after_spec <-meanspec(After_event, f=300000, ovlp=90, plot=FALSE, dB=NULL, norm=FALSE)

And then I will test for differences between these extracted spectra.

Two questions:
1. I have not been able to find the units for the data frame returned by mean spec. Is the unit mV?
2. I would like the returned value to represent absolute energy in each frequency bin over the duration of the recording. I have tried to write the code in a way that achieves this without normalization, but if this is not correct, I would be very grateful to know.

Thank you very much for your time, thoughts, and suggestions,
Laurel

messages.author: de80047cbc18c87e
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] meanspec() units and usage
parts: 1. I have not been able to find the units for the data frame returned by mean spec. Is the unit mV?

No, there are no units. If you add correction="amplitude" (I alsor remove dB=NULL which is a default seeting), you should have values that correspond to the amplitude values of your original sound, along a 2^16 scale if your file was digitized with a 16 bit depth.

before_spec<-meanspec(Before_event, f=300000, ovlp=90, plot=FALSE, correction="amplitude", norm=FALSE)
after_spec <-meanspec(After_event, f=300000, ovlp=90, plot=FALSE, correction="amplitude", norm=FALSE)

2. I would like the returned value to represent absolute energy in each frequency bin over the duration of the recording. I have tried to write the code in a way that achieves this without normalization, but if this is not correct, I would be very grateful to know.

I think that the code above should do the job. But be aware that meanspec() computes an average of your data so that you transform in a certain way your data.

HTH

Jerome
